cases.task: Given the deliberately supplied FILE-pointer control, determine which bytes reach the file before observation and which operation triggers them. Compare controlled+flush, controlled without flush and ordinary+flush. Distinguish a stream effect from PC control.
Recover the callbacks reached by return, exit, quick_exit and immediate termination. Give native controls and distinguish real callback dispatch from corruption of an internal exit list.
Identify the opened descriptor and installed filter, explain the feasible file-I/O path, and contrast read with denied open. Keep architecture, filter provenance and observed native results explicit.
Investigate allocation aliases and resize-to-zero state. Demonstrate only the reachable stale-alias effect, compare default allocation with disabled tcache, and state runtime/reuse prerequisites.

Recover the input grammar and decoded size/distance checks. Build a valid input and one bounded violation that changes the adjacent protected field. Establish the root cause without upgrading the state change to code execution.

Recover logical object references across collection/reuse and compare a live-reference control. Establish whether a stale logical handle changes the reused object, distinguishing this from a native arbitrary write.
Compare valid, embedded-NUL and invalid UTF-8 input. Recover exact output bytes and borrowed/owned behavior. Explain why buffer identity matters for a later pointer-dependent operation.
Recover the numeric input representation and exact resulting bits. Test a finite value, negative zero and NaN payload preservation. Do not use numeric equality to certify byte identity.

Identify the supplied static runtime and determine the observed positional-format behavior. Use the result to assess the claim that musl universally lacks dollar positional formats; bound conclusions to the actual build.
